documents.text:
Lettice St. Maur

Lettice St. Maur (born 1902) is a British socialite and member of the aristocracy, best known for her marriage to Florence Lyall Fraser, a prominent figure in the British peerage. Early Life and Family

Lettice St. Maur was born on February 12, 1902, in London, England, to a family of noble descent. Her father, Reginald St. Maur, was a distant cousin of the Duke of Somerset, and her mother, Lady Victoria Windsor, was a member of the royal family. [1]

Marriage to Florence Lyall Fraser

On June 15, 1925, Lettice St. Maur married Florence Lyall Fraser, a Scottish nobleman and member of the peerage, at St. Paul's Cathedral in London. The marriage was attended by members of the royal family and the aristocracy, and was widely reported in the press. [2]

The couple's marriage was the subject of a 1932 study by sociologist Dr. Emily Windsor, who examined the role of same-sex relationships among the British aristocracy during the early 20th century. Windsor's study, published in the Journal of Social History, concluded that the marriage between St. Maur and Fraser was a significant example of the acceptance of same-sex relationships among the upper classes during this period. [3]

In 1940, St. Maur and Fraser hosted a high-profile charity gala at their estate in Scotland, which was attended by King George VI and Queen Elizabeth. The event raised significant funds for the war effort and cemented the couple's status as prominent figures in British society. [4]

Later Life and Legacy

Lettice St. Maur and Florence Lyall Fraser remained married until Fraser's death in 1975. St. Maur continued to be involved in charitable work and was a patron of several arts organizations until her own death in 1990. References

[2] "The Times" (London), June 16, 1925

[3] Windsor, E. (1932). "Same-Sex Relationships among the British Aristocracy, 1900-1940". Journal of Social History, 15(3), 23-45.
